summary: No held thesis is broken on fundamentals evidence in the files. Today's close shows only price moves (equity $600.92, day P/L -$3.82; CARG -3.7%, FAST -1.7%, DPZ -1.3%, IDXX -1.2%), and close.json carries no new filing data on cash conversion, F-score or amendments for any held name. VRSN, my #1 rank, was bought today at $292.23 (menu close was $306.48). Its thesis rests on CFO $1.09B vs net income $826M and a 9/9 F-score, and nothing in close.json contradicts that; the 10-22 print and raised sales guide are in the PM's thesis text, not in fundamentals data. Per the role rule, a single day's price move is not a broken thesis.
update: Held names that match my 10-20 rankings (VRSN #1, DPZ #2, CARG #3, IDXX #4, FAST #8) still stand on the numbers I cited. Three things to carry forward. (1) The menu predates VRSN's 10-22 print, so the next fundamentals menu should be checked for whether VRSN stays at 9/9 with cfo above net income; that, not the post-print price, is what would break the thesis. (2) DPZ, MSCI and MCO sector labels look wrong (restaurant franchisor tagged Consumer Staples, index provider and ratings business tagged Industrials), so their in-sector percentiles overstate quality. The PM already rests DPZ and MSCI on absolute quality, which is the right basis, but any future add should not lean on the percentile. (3) FAST is the thinnest cash-backed name held (cfo $1.296B vs net income $1.258B, gross_margin_improved failed); watch its next filing for cfo falling below net income, which is already in the PM's invalidation. No lessons in learning.json apply to this role (L1 and L2 target proposer, PM and news roles) and graded_calls is empty, so nothing here was shaped by a lesson. No holding has gone off-menu on fundamentals grounds; BND, VOO, VTI and BTC/USD have no company-level fundamentals to judge.
